Skip next section Israeli military acknowledges marking detained Palestinians with numbers 08/18/2026 August 18, 2026 Israeli military acknowledges marking detained Palestinians with numbers The Israeli military on Tuesday acknowledged that soldiers carrying out a raid in the northern West Bank on Monday had marked detained Palestinians with numbers. In a statement to The Times of Israel newspaper, the military said the seriousness of the conduct had been stressed to the troops involved and that "lessons have been learned." Footage emerged on Monday showing a Palestinian man speaking to local media after being questioned by Israeli soldiers, with the number 44 written across his forehead. The man said the troops had marked others who were questioned. The measure has long been considered taboo in Israel, as it is reminiscent of the numbered tattoos which Germany's Nazi regime used to identify concentration and death camp inmates during the Holocaust . Earlier in April, footage showed Palestinian women with numbers written on their hands after they were briefly allowed to enter the Israeli military-controlled Jenin refugee camp to collect their belongings. In response to the footage, the Israeli military acknowledged the incident and said "lessons have been learned," echoing a similar statement to the one issued on Tuesday. The UNIFIL in southern Lebanon has been in place since 1978 to confirm Israeli withdrawal from the Arab country. It has some 7,500 personnel from nearly 50 countries. Despite its presence, Lebanon has seen various wars between Israel and the pro-Iranian Hezbollah group, as well as Israeli ground invasions. In August last year, the UN Security Council decided to end UNIFIL's mandate on December 31, 2026, amid growing US pressure. "Pulling the plug on UNIFIL without a robust international force in place would effectively abandon millions of Lebanese civilians to an uncertain and potentially disastrous fate," said Louis Charbonneau, HRW's UN director said in a statement issued last week. "The peacekeepers are a crucial deterrent against attacks on civilians and human rights abuses," he added. HRW argued that since the decision to end UNIFIL's mandate preceded this year's war and the subsequent Israeli invasion of southern Lebanon, the decision should be revised. Hezbollah dragged Lebanon into the wider Middle East conflict on March 2 when it attacked Israel, in retaliation for US and Israeli attacks on Iran. This led to a wide Israeli bombing campaign and a ground invasion which has killed over 4,300 people in Lebanon.
